free_tier.stated: 5 hours / 500 MB TOTAL, not monthly: 'Total storage: 5 hours (500MB). Note: Storage does not reset monthly.' Help centre adds: 'The total file size should not exceed 500MB' and 'The total length of the file should not exceed 5 hours'. Both accumulate and block further uploads when either is hit.

egress.terms: 100 GB per month on Free ('Monthly bandwidth: 100GB'), unmetered beyond that in the sense of no per-GB charge but the account stalls at the cap. Paid Unlimited Audio ($12/mo) is 'Unmetered bandwidth'.

record.tooling: No public upload API on Free (Podbean developer docs exist for read/embed; upload is dashboard). Migration-in by RSS is one click and is explicitly free, which is a heavier hammer than a per-episode upload.
record.chaining: 5 hours / 500 MB per free account, 100 GB/mo bandwidth. At ~128 kbps that is ~9 hours of audio; at 500 MB hard cap the file-size ceiling bites first for anything lossless. Genuinely small. Only interesting multiplied across many accounts, and each account needs an email + verification.
record.limits_note: 3 episodes/day; 100 MB single file on Free (3 GB on paid); RSS feed exposes only the most recent 20 episodes on Free; formats on Free are MP3 and M4A only (paid adds ogg/zip/pdf/pptx/docx/xml. Note zip is a paid-plan format, so Free cannot take archives at all).
record.reliability_note: Likely re-encodes. Verified live: enclosure https://mcdn.podbean.com/mf/web/rhvxkzpmimms9sf5/riverside_....mp3 -> 302 -> 206, Content-Range 0-1023/73948726; declared length 73948726 for a 3081 s episode = 191,988 bps, i.e. exactly 192 kbps CBR, and the ID3 tag names Lavf60.16.1 (ffmpeg) as the encoder. The upload was a 'riverside_..._processed.mp3' (Riverside's own processed export, normally 128 kbps), so 192k suggests Podbean re-encoded upward rather than storing as-is — unverified without an account, but the ffmpeg stamp plus exact CBR strongly implies server-side processing.
